mainTopic: Stories of unexpected wealth and of תורה in plain 'vessels', the explanation of the ביצה טורמיטא and כלופסין, and stories about רבי and בר קפרא.
overview: The גמרא finishes its list of the people through whom רבי עקיבא became rich. It then tells how רב גמדא's 'wasted' purchase of a monkey led him to a pile of pearls. Next, בת קיסר mocks רבי יהושע בן חנניה as an ugly vessel for beautiful תורה. He answers with the example of wine, which spoils in silver and gold. A woman who describes שמואל's looks in a mocking way is put in שמתא by רב יהודה and dies. The גמרא then returns to our משנה and explains the ביצה טורמיטא, a specially shrunk egg that doctors use. It also explains the word כלופסין, a kind of fig used for cooked dishes, and tells a story about a thousand kinds of fig dishes. The amud ends with stories about רבי's great wealth and his witty student-colleague בר קפרא, and that last story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two more sources of רבי עקיבא's wealth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its list of the sources of רבי עקיבא's wealth: the wife of טורנוסרופוס and קטיעא בר שלום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא also became rich from the wife of טורנוסרופוס, and from קטיעא בר שלום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list it started earlier, naming the last two people through whom רבי עקיבא became wealthy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only makes sense as the end of an earlier list of the sources of רבי עקיבא's wealth. Both people named here were Romans. The point is that his wealth came to him in surprising ways.

keyTerms.meaning: Turnus Rufus, a Roman governor of Judea
Ketia bar Shalom, a Roman official

phrases.english: And from the wife of Turnus Rufus,
and from Ketia bar Shalom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a list that began before this text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's wealth also came from the wife of טורנוסרופוס and from קטיעא בר שלום.

steps.title: רב גמדא, the monkey, and the pearls
steps.stepSummary: רב גמדא paid sailors to bring him something. They brought a monkey, and the monkey led them to a hidden store of pearls.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גמדא gave four זוזים to sailors so they would buy him something with them. They found nothing worth buying, so they brought him a monkey. The monkey ran off into a hole. They dug after it, found it crouching on pearls, and brought all the pearls to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story of a חכם who became rich in an unexpected way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It looked as if רב גמדא had wasted his money on a monkey. The 'worthless' purchase turned into a fortune when the monkey's hiding place held pearls. This fits the theme of the previous step: wealth reaching תלמידי חכמים in surprising ways.

keyTerms.meaning: zuz coins, a kind of silver coin

phrases.english: Rav Gamda gave four zuz
to sailors, to bring him something with them.
They did not find anything,
so they brought him a monkey with the money.
It slipped away and went into a hole.
They dug after it,
and found it crouching on pearls,
and they brought all of them to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב גַּמָּדָא יְהֵיב אַרְבָּעָה זוּזִי לְסָפוֹנָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about a חכם becoming rich in an unexpected way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב גמדא's small, seemingly wasted purchase led to a fortune in pearls.

steps.title: The emperor's daughter mocks רבי יהושע's appearance
steps.stepSummary: בת קיסר tells רבי יהושע בן חנניה that he is glorious תורה inside an ugly vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: The emperor's daughter said to רבי יהושע בן חנניה: Magnificent תורה in an ugly vessel!
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. בת קיסר makes a cutting remark that רבי יהושע בן חנניה, who was not good-looking, is an ugly container for beautiful תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her remark works like a challenge: why would such great wisdom sit in such a plain-looking person? The next steps show how he answers it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ בַּת קֵיסָר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה:
phrases.english: The emperor's daughter said to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ḥananya:
Magnificent Torah in an ugly vessel!
phrases.notes: The 'ugly vessel' is רבי יהושע himself. She is insulting his looks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ בַּת קֵיסָר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, separate story.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fit between great תורה and an unattractive person.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something so glorious should be kept in a beautiful container, so why is it held in someone so plain?

steps.title: רבי יהושע asks where the palace keeps its wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע asks her where the palace stores its wine. She says in clay jars, and he tells her royalty should use silver and gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: Learn from your father's house. What do you keep wine in? She said: In clay vessels. He said: Everyone keeps wine in clay, and you do too?! You should put it in vessels of silver and gold!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע doesn't answer her directly yet. He is setting up a test with the palace wine that will prove his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses her own logic against her: if fine things belong in fine containers, the royal wine should be in silver and gold. He knows what will happen, and the result will be his real answer in the next step.

phrases.english: He said to her: Learn from your father's house.
What do you keep wine in?
She said to him: In clay vessels.
He said to her: Everyone keeps it in clay,
and you keep it in clay vessels too?!
phrases.notes: He means: you are royalty, so shouldn't your wine be stored better than everyone else's?

phrases.english: You should put it in vessels of silver and gold!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins רבי יהושע's response to her taunt by setting up a demonstration.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An indirect answer: he gets her to test fancy containers on the palace wine.

steps.title: The wine spoils, and so does תורה
steps.stepSummary: She moves the wine into silver and gold, and it spoils. רבי יהושע says the same is true of תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: She went and put the wine in vessels of silver and gold, and it went sour. He said to her: The same is true of the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The test is done: the wine spoiled in the fancy vessels. רבי יהושע now gives his answer, that תורה also keeps best in a plain 'vessel'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine keeps well in simple clay and spoils in precious metal. In the same way, תורה lasts better in a plain-looking person, while good looks can spoil it. This turns her insult into a lesson.
steps.whatToRemember: Just as wine keeps best in plain clay, תורה keeps best in a plain, humble 'vessel'.

phrases.english: She went and put the wine
in vessels of silver and gold, and it went sour.
He said to her: The Torah is the same way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַלַת וּרְמָת חַמְרָא בְּמָאנֵי דְּכַסְפָּא וְדַהֲבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the demonstration set up in step 4 and applies it to תורה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Glorious things belong in beautiful containers, so a great חכם should be handsome.
steps.terutzMaskana: Precious things like wine and תורה keep best in plain vessels, so a plain appearance actually suits תורה.

steps.title: But some people are handsome and learned
steps.stepSummary: She objects that there are people who are both good-looking and learned in תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are people who are handsome and learned!
steps.whatsHappening: בת קיסר pushes back on his answer by pointing to good-looking people who are still great in תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If good looks spoil תורה the way silver spoils wine, handsome people should not be learned. She says real life shows otherwise, which seems to break his comparison.

phrases.english: But there are people who are handsome and learned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the lesson drawn in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that good looks spoil תורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexamples: some people are both good-looking and learned, so beauty does not seem to ruin תורה.

steps.title: They would be even more learned if they were plain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers that those handsome scholars would have learned even more if they were ugly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: If they were ugly, they would be even more learned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers her objection, and the story ends here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not deny that handsome scholars exist. He says their looks still cost them something, and plain looks would have let them learn even more. So his comparison to wine still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: Handsome scholars exist, but according to רבי יהושע they would have been even greater if they were plain. Humility and plainness help תורה last.

phrases.english: He said to her: If they were ugly,
they would be even more learned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the facts but limits the claim
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Handsome learned people show that beauty does not harm תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Beauty still holds them back. If they were plain, they would have learned more.

steps.title: A woman loses her case before רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A woman comes to רב יהודה of נהרדעא for a court case and loses.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain woman came before רב יהודה of נהרדעא for judgment, and she lost the case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story. This line only sets the scene for what she says next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier story about רבי יהושע, this story will turn on someone's looks. Here, though, the comments about appearance come across as an insult to a תלמיד חכם.

keyTerms.meaning: for judgment, for a court case
she was found liable, she lost the case
נהרדעא, a major Jewish city in Babylonia

phrases.english: A certain woman who came before
Rav Yehuda of Neharde'a for judgment
and she was found guilty in the judgment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story that follows the earlier one about appearance and תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the scene: a woman loses her case before רב יהודה.

steps.title: She protests that שמואל would not have ruled this way
steps.stepSummary: The woman challenges the ruling by appealing to רב יהודה's teacher, שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: Would שמואל your teacher have judged us like this?!
steps.whatsHappening: The woman objects to the ruling. She claims that רב יהודה's own teacher would have decided differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her challenge is aimed at the ruling itself. She suggests that רב יהודה is not following the way his רבי judged.

phrases.english: She said to him: Shmuel your teacher,
would he have judged us like this?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Her reaction to losing the case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She claims his teacher שמואל would have ruled differently.

steps.title: רב יהודה asks if she knew שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה asks whether she actually knew שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: Did you know him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה asks a short question. It sets up her answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is testing whether she can really speak about how שמואל judged.

phrases.english: He said to her: Did you know him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to her challenge with a question.

steps.title: She describes שמואל in unflattering terms
steps.stepSummary: She says yes, and describes שמואל as short, potbellied, dark, with large teeth.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: Yes. He was short with a big belly, dark, with big teeth.
steps.whatsHappening: She answers that she knew him, and to prove it she describes how he looked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of saying something about his wisdom or his rulings, she points to his physical flaws. The way she describes a great חכם comes across as mocking.

phrases.english: She said to him: Yes,
short and his belly is big,
dark and his teeth are big.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יהודה's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, and she describes שמואל's looks in an insulting way.

steps.title: רב יהודה puts her in שמתא and she dies
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says she came to insult שמואל and excommunicates her. She bursts and dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: Did you come to insult him? Let that woman be in excommunication. She burst open and died.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה sees her description as an insult to his teacher and puts her in שמתא. She is punished immediately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her real offense is not losing the case or arguing about it. It is belittling a תלמיד חכם. Her sudden death shows how serious it is to disgrace a חכם.

keyTerms.meaning: to disgrace him, to insult him

steps.whatToRemember: Insulting a תלמיד חכם is treated with great severity.

phrases.english: He said to her: Did you come to disgrace him?
Let that woman be under a ban.
She burst open and died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב יהודה reacts to her description.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Disgracing a תלמיד חכם brings severe punishment.

steps.title: What is a ביצה טורמיטא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to our משנה and asks what a ביצה טורמיטא is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says he is permitted to eat a ביצה טורמיטא. What is a ביצה טורמיטא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to our משנה. It quotes the line about the special egg and asks what that egg is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who vowed off 'cooked food' is still allowed this egg. To understand why, we first need to know what the egg is and how it is made.

keyTerms.meaning: a specially prepared egg (explained in the next step)

phrases.english: And he is permitted to eat a turemita egg.
phrases.notes: This line is quoted from our משנה about someone who made a vow not to eat cooked food.

phrases.english: What is a turemita egg?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and goes back to explaining the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the term ביצה טורמיטא.

steps.title: שמואל explains how the egg is made and used
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the egg is dipped in hot and cold water until it shrinks enough to swallow whole. Doctors use it to find internal sores.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: A slave who knows how to make it is worth a thousand דינרים. He dips it a thousand times in hot water and a thousand times in cold water until it shrinks, so that a person can swallow it whole. If there is a sore inside, it sticks to the egg. When the egg comes out, the doctor knows what medicine is needed and how the person can be healed.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל describes how the special egg is prepared and why it is so valuable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The egg is shrunk by dipping it again and again in hot and cold water until it can be swallowed whole. Its main use is medical: if there is a sore inside, part of it sticks to the egg, and when the egg comes out the doctor knows what medicine is needed.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
A slave who knows how to make it
is worth a thousand dinars,

phrases.aramaic: וּמְעַיֵּיל לַהּ אַלְפָּא זִימְנֵי בְּמַיָּא חַמִּימֵי
phrases.english: and he puts it a thousand times into hot water
and a thousand times into cold water
until it shrinks,
so that one can swallow it whole,
and if there is a sore inside, it sticks to it,
and when it comes out,

phrases.aramaic: יָדַע אָסְיָא מַאי סַמָּא מִתְבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
phrases.english: the doctor knows what medicine he needs
and with what he can be healed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: עַבְדָּא דְּעָבֵיד לַהּ שָׁוֵי אַלְפָּא דִּינָרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about what the egg is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is an egg shrunk by repeated hot and cold dipping, used by doctors to find internal sores.

steps.title: שמואל tests himself with a stalk
steps.stepSummary: שמואל used to examine himself with a vegetable stalk, until his family tore their hair out in worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל would examine himself with a stalk, until the people of his household would tear out their hair over him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short story about שמואל himself doing a similar medical check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the medical use of the egg in the last step. The test was so hard on his body that his family thought he was in danger.

phrases.english: Shmuel would examine himself with a stalk,
until the members of his household would tear out
their hair over him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related story about a medical self-examination.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל examined himself with a stalk, at great physical cost.

steps.title: A משנה about a worker and two kinds of figs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a worker handling כלופסין may not eat בנות שבע, and a worker handling בנות שבע may not eat כלופסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: If he was working with כלופסין, he may not eat from בנות שבע. If he was working with בנות שבע, he may not eat from כלופסין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from elsewhere that treats two kinds of figs as different foods. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though both are figs, a worker may only eat the kind he is working with. Like our vow case, this shows that different kinds of the same food can be treated separately.

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in מעשרות 2:8.

phrases.english: If he was working with keloppasin,
he may not eat from benot sheva.
If with benot sheva, he may not eat from keloppasin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source about different kinds of the same food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A worker may eat only the specific kind of fig he is working with.

steps.title: What are כלופסין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word כלופסין means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are כלופסין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of an unfamiliar word in the משנה it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the rule can be understood, we need to know which fruit the משנה is talking about.

phrases.english: What are keloppasin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the quoted משנה.

steps.title: כלופסין are figs used for cooked fruit
steps.stepSummary: כלופסין are a kind of fig from which a cooked fruit dish is made.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are a kind of fig from which they make a cooked fruit dish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that כלופסין are a type of fig used to make a cooked fruit dish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know that כלופסין are a separate variety of fig. That is why a worker handling one kind may not eat the other.

keyTerms.meaning: a cooked fruit dish, like a compote

phrases.english: A kind of figs
from which they make compote.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the word.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A variety of fig used to make a cooked fruit dish.

steps.title: A lawsuit over a thousand kinds of fig dishes
steps.stepSummary: A man gave his slave to his friend to be taught a thousand kinds of fig dishes. The friend taught only eight hundred, so the man took him to court before רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who gave his slave to a friend to teach him a thousand kinds of fig dishes. The friend taught him only eight hundred, and the man brought him to court before רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story connected to the fig dishes it just mentioned. This sets up רבי's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 explained that כלופסין are figs used for cooked dishes. This story shows how many such dishes existed. The court case itself is only background for what רבי says next.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who gave a slave to his friend
to teach him a thousand kinds of fig dishes.
He taught him eight hundred.
He summoned him to court before Rabbi.
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no other name always means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Story tied to the fig dishes defined in step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: a court case over teaching 1,000 kinds of fig dishes, of which only 800 were taught.

steps.title: רבי is amazed: we never even saw such good things
steps.stepSummary: רבי says that our ancestors at least forgot good times they once had, but we have never even seen such luxury.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: Our ancestors said, "We have forgotten what good is." We have not even seen it with our own eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי reacts to the case with surprise. He had never imagined there could be so many kinds of fig dishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי quotes a פסוק where earlier generations complain that they forgot the good times. His point is that they at least once had those good times. His own generation never even saw that kind of plenty, so even eight hundred dishes amazes him.

keyTerms.meaning: We have forgotten what good is (a phrase from a פסוק)

phrases.english: Rabbi said:
Our forefathers said: "We have forgotten what good is."
We have not even seen it with our own eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי's reaction that ends the story from step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Earlier generations once enjoyed such plenty. Ours never saw it.

steps.title: A hugely expensive wedding, and בר קפרא is not invited
steps.stepSummary: רבי made a wedding for his son רבי שמעון. The canopy was marked as costing an enormous sum, and בר קפרא was not invited.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי made a wedding for his son רבי שמעון. Written on the canopy was: "Twenty-four thousand myriads of dinars were spent on this canopy." And רבי did not invite בר קפרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story showing רבי's great wealth. This sets up בר קפרא's sharp remark in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the huge number is to show how rich רבי was. Leaving out בר קפרא is the key detail, because his insulted response comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A student-colleague of רבי, famous for his wit

phrases.english: Rabbi made a wedding feast
for Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi.
Written on the canopy was:
Twenty-four thousand myriads of dinars
were spent on this canopy.
And he did not invite bar Kappara.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲבַד לֵיהּ הִלּוּלָא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about רבי's wealth, linked by the theme of luxury
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: a lavish wedding without בר קפרא.

steps.title: בר קפרא's sharp remark about reward
steps.stepSummary: The uninvited בר קפרא hints at רבי's wrong: if people who go against God's will are rewarded this richly, those who do His will must be rewarded even more.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא said to רבי: If those who go against God's will get this much, then those who do His will, how much more so!
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא, insulted, uses a קל וחומר as a hidden jab at רבי for not inviting him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By pointing to רבי's own wealth as the reward of "those who go against His will," בר קפרא hints that רבי did wrong by leaving him out. The קל וחומר goes from less deserving to more deserving: if wrongdoers get such wealth, the righteous surely get more.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who go against God's will
How much more so (the wording of a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: בר קפרא is the one speaking here, and he is talking to רבי.

phrases.english: If those who go against His will get this much,

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹשֵׂי רְצוֹנוֹ עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה.
phrases.english: then those who do His will, how much more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: בר קפרא responds to being left out in step 21
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קל וחומר from the wealth of wrongdoers to the reward of the righteous, said as a jab.

steps.title: After being invited, בר קפרא changes his קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי invites בר קפרא, who then reshapes his remark as praise: if the righteous get this much in this world, they will get even more in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי invited him. בר קפרא then said: If those who do His will get this much in this world, how much more so in עולם הבא!
steps.whatsHappening: Once he is invited, בר קפרא turns his jab into a compliment. This ends the wedding story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי is counted among those who do God's will, not those who go against it. The קל וחומר now goes from this world to עולם הבא: if this is the reward here, the reward in the next world must be far greater.

phrases.english: He invited him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: לְעוֹשֵׂי רְצוֹנוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כָּךְ
phrases.english: He said: If those who do His will get this much in this world,

phrases.aramaic: לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה.
phrases.english: how much more so in the World to Come!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַזְמְנֵיהּ, אֲמַר: לְעוֹשֵׂי רְצוֹנוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the jab of step 22 into praise once בר קפרא is invited
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The righteous will get far more in עולם הבא than the great wealth they have here.
steps.whatToRemember: The same קל וחומר shape is used twice: first as an insult (step 22), then as praise (step 23). The only thing that changed is whether בר קפרא was invited.

steps.title: רבי asks בר קפרא not to make him laugh
steps.stepSummary: On days when רבי laughed, trouble came to the world. So רבי offered בר קפרא forty measures of wheat not to make him laugh.
steps.simpleTranslation: On any day that רבי laughed, calamity came to the world. So he said to בר קפרא: Do not make me laugh, and I will give you forty סאה of wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins another story about רבי and בר קפרא. It gives the background and רבי's offer, setting up בר קפרא's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The text says a day when רבי laughed brought trouble to the world, so רבי wanted to avoid laughing. Since בר קפרא was known as a joker, רבי offered to pay him to hold back.

phrases.english: On a day when Rabbi laughed,
calamity came to the world.
He said to bar Kappara:
Do not make me laugh,
and I will give you forty se'ah of wheat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story about the same two people
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי offers בר קפרא forty se'ah of wheat not to make him laugh.

steps.title: בר קפרא begins his reply
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא starts to answer רבי's offer with "Let the Master see." The rest of his reply continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא said to him: Let the Master see...
steps.whatsHappening: This is only the opening of בר קפרא's answer. The גמרא is setting up the next move, and the rest of his reply comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing has been decided yet. Keep רבי's offer from step 24 in mind, because בר קפרא's answer is responding to it.

phrases.english: He said to him: Let the Master see

steps.relationToPreviousStep: בר קפרא begins answering רבי's offer from step 24
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening words of בר קפרא's reply, continued next.
